title: Keyboard Manager Exchange CTRL and WIN to cause third-party software unworking

status.label: Retest Ctrl/Win swap with the translator
status.detail: The reporter attached a PowerToys report and KeyViz observation showing Ctrl+Win+C after a Ctrl/Win swap; the reported build is v0.74.1.

judgment.rationale: The report lists PowerToys v0.74.1, gives the Ctrl/Win exchange and Win+C sequence, and explains how the resulting Ctrl+Win+C activates a Teams shortcut instead of the third-party TTime translator's copy action. A collaborator requested /bugreport and the author supplied a PowerToys report ZIP, then described the same observed key combination in KeyViz, so another archive request is unnecessary. The behavior is old and no current-build confirmation or linked PR was found; verify it on v0.102.3001 before deciding whether the remap still emits the source modifier.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys v0.74.1 and says exchanging Ctrl and Win makes the translator fail.
The reporter states that Win+C produces Ctrl+Win+C and that KeyViz showed this combination.
The author attached a PowerToys report ZIP after a collaborator requested /bugreport.
The issue has two comments, no assignee, and no matching PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the reciprocal Ctrl/Win remap on v0.102.3001 and verify whether Win+C still emits both the source and remapped modifiers before designing a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported key sequence is consistent with the source Win modifier not being fully suppressed during a reciprocal Ctrl/Win remap, but the observation is from v0.74.1 and has not been independently reproduced on current stable.

proposed_fixes.title: Suppress the source modifier during reciprocal Ctrl/Win remapping
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A reciprocal Ctrl/Win key exchange may inject the target modifier while allowing the original modifier to reach the application, producing Ctrl+Win+C instead of the expected single remapped chord. The current-build behavior is unconfirmed.
plan: Reproduce the exact reciprocal Ctrl/Win exchange on the current supported build and record the modifier sequence for Win+C.
Trace source-key suppression and target modifier key-down/key-up handling for the confirmed mapping.
Ensure the original modifier is suppressed while the remapped modifier remains held for the source key's lifetime.
Add regression coverage for reciprocal Ctrl/Win remaps and for ordinary Ctrl/Win shortcuts that are not configured for remapping.
verification: Verify Win+C after the reciprocal exchange produces only the expected remapped chord and no unintended Teams/system shortcut.
Verify the reporter's TTime copy/translation workflow and normal Ctrl/Win shortcuts remain functional.

confidence.rationale: The attached report and KeyViz description point to a modifier-suppression issue, but the product version is old and the emitted sequence has not been confirmed on current stable.

issue_context.summary: A reciprocal Ctrl/Win key exchange reportedly makes Win+C emit Ctrl+Win+C, which conflicts with the TTime translator's copy shortcut.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys v0.74.1 and says Ctrl and Win are exchanged in Keyboard Manager.
The reporter says the translator uses Copy to capture underlined text and that Win+C instead produces Ctrl+Win+C, activating Teams.
The reporter says KeyViz observed Ctrl+Win+C and attached a PowerToys report ZIP after a collaborator requested /bugreport.
The issue has no assignee and no matching PR was found.
inferences: The original Win modifier may be reaching the target application alongside the remapped Ctrl modifier, but the event sequence has not been verified on current stable.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied archive and KeyViz observation are useful evidence and should not be requested again. The exact reciprocal mapping is clear enough for a maintainer reproduction, but the report is from v0.74.1 and the current behavior is unknown. Search found an older Win/Alt shortcut report (#5956), but it does not cover this Ctrl/Win exchange or establish a fix.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and both comments, including the original /bugreport request, the attached archive, and the author's KeyViz explanation.
Searched for reports containing the reported Ctrl+Win+C sequence; no other direct matching issue was found.
Searched for PRs referencing the issue; none were returned.

information_gaps.information: Whether Win+C still produces Ctrl+Win+C on v0.102.3001 with the same reciprocal Ctrl/Win mapping, and whether TTime still fails
information_gaps.why_needed: The only versioned reproduction is v0.74.1; a current retest determines whether the source modifier is still leaking or whether a later change already fixed the behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001, keep the same Ctrl/Win exchange, test Win+C with a key-event viewer such as the reporter's KeyViz setup, and report the observed chord and whether TTime still performs its copy/translation action.

actions.label: Retest the Ctrl/Win swap on current stable

comment.body: Thanks for providing the PowerToys report ZIP and the KeyViz observation that Win+C produced Ctrl+Win+C; the archive should not need to be uploaded again. Since the report is from v0.74.1, could you confirm whether this still happens on v0.102.3001 with the same reciprocal Ctrl/Win mapping? Please report the chord shown by KeyViz and whether TTime still fails to copy and translate the selected text.

actions.label: Reproduce the Ctrl/Win modifier exchange
actions.note: The report includes the exact mapping and a diagnostic archive; verify the modifier sequence on current stable before choosing a code path.

reproduce.title: Verify reciprocal Ctrl/Win remapping
prerequisites: A reciprocal Ctrl/Win key remap configured in Keyboard Manager
A text editor or key-event viewer to observe the emitted chord
steps: Configure the same Ctrl/Win exchange described in the issue.
Press Win+C and record whether the application receives Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Win+C, or another sequence.
If available, repeat in TTime and verify whether its Copy-based translation action still works.
reproduce.expected_result: The remapping produces only the intended target modifier and does not also expose the original source modifier to the application.
